title: FedRAMP 20x Readiness Check
line: 10 questions, one for each theme of the Key Security Indicators. About three minutes.
honest: A self-check. Your answers stay on this device and nobody else sees them. It is not a FedRAMP assessment, and it does not stand in for a FedRAMP Recognized assessor.

items.question: Does everyone who works on the service get security training, and is all of that training reviewed and kept current?
items.next: Review all security training on a schedule, and keep the record of each review.

items.question: Is every change to the service logged and validated on its way to production, by redeploying where you can instead of modifying in place?
items.next: Log every change, validate it throughout deployment, and prefer redeploying to modifying.

items.question: Does each part of the service have a defined function and privileges, with network traffic restricted and the intended state enforced?
items.next: Define each component’s function and privileges, restrict the traffic between them, and enforce the intended state.

items.question: Do accounts follow least privilege, with passwordless sign-in where you can, just-in-time authorization and secured authentication for what is not a person?
items.next: Automate account management, adopt passwordless methods, and authorize privileged access just in time.

items.question: Do you review your incident response procedures and your past incidents, and write an after action report for each incident?
items.next: Review the incident response procedures and past incidents, and write an after action report for the next one.

items.question: Are the event types that matter logged, reviewed and sent to a security information and event management capability, with access to the logs authorized?
items.next: Decide which event types to log, send them to one place, review them, and authorize who may read them.

items.question: Do you keep current inventories, and can you show executive support, investment in security, security in the development life cycle and a way to receive vulnerability disclosures?
items.next: Generate the inventories, then gather what shows executive support, investment and security in the development life cycle.

items.question: Are recovery objectives set and reviewed, backups aligned to them, and recovery tested?
items.next: Set the recovery objectives, align the backups and the recovery plan to them, and test a recovery.

items.question: Do you monitor the risk your suppliers bring and act to reduce it?
items.next: List the suppliers the service depends on, and decide how you monitor and reduce the risk from each.

items.question: Are configuration and secrets managed by automation, communications and resources validated, and unwanted data removed?
items.next: Automate configuration and secret management, validate communications and resource integrity, and remove data you do not need.
